# Export feature
FR-03: The system must let an authenticated analyst export the visible report.
UC-03 Export report: analyst clicks Export; system creates a CSV.
Entity mapping: FR-03 -> Report.
Traceability: FR-03 -> UC-03 -> Report.
The document contains no export success criterion, size/timeout rule, authorization failure path, empty-report behavior, or Given/When/Then acceptance scenario.

FR-01 Customer creates ticket; FR-02 Agent assigns priority; FR-03 Customer closes own ticket. UC-01/02/03 map one-to-one. Entities: Ticket maps FR-01 and FR-03; Priority and Ticket map FR-02. S-01 Given authenticated customer, when valid ticket is submitted, then ID appears within 2s. S-02 Given assigned agent, when priority P1-P3 is selected, then it is recorded; unauthorized user is denied. S-03 Given ticket owner and open ticket, when Close is confirmed, then status and timestamp persist; non-owner and already-closed attempts are rejected. Traceability rows map every FR to its actor, UC, entities, positive/negative scenario, and measurable UAT result.

// billing/invoice-service.ts imports {OrderService} from '../orders/order-service' to calculate totals. // orders/order-service.ts imports {InvoiceService} from '../billing/invoice-service' to read payment state. Both services construct the other in their default constructors and invoke synchronous callbacks after updates. No port, event contract, or composition-root boundary exists.

Orders owns Order and publishes OrderConfirmed.v1 through a transactional outbox. Billing consumes the versioned integration event into its own PaymentRequest model and publishes PaymentAccepted.v1. Neither context imports the other's domain classes or database. JSON schemas are versioned; producer and consumer contract tests run in CI; handlers are idempotent by eventId; retries go to a dead-letter queue with alerts.

router.patch('/users/:id', requireAdmin, async (req,res) => { const user = await prisma.user.update({where:{id:req.params.id}, data:req.body}); res.json(user); }); The accepted JSON is not schema-validated or field-allowlisted and may include role, tenantId, passwordHash, isActive, and createdAt.

POST /webhooks/payment reads at most 256KB raw bytes, verifies HMAC over the raw body with constant-time comparison before JSON parsing, and rejects signatures older than 5 minutes. Secret is referenced only as PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Event ID has a unique constraint; duplicate delivery returns prior success. Validated event types map to allowlisted commands. Tests cover invalid signature, modified body, stale timestamp, oversized body, unknown type, replay, and valid delivery.

Delete confirmation modal handoff specifies a centered 480px panel, title, warning copy, Cancel and Delete buttons, overlay color, and destructive-button hover state. It contains no accessible name/description mapping, initial focus, focus trap, Tab order, Escape behavior, focus restoration, keyboard activation, or screen-reader announcement guidance.

Dashboard handoff defines semantic color/type/spacing/radius/elevation/motion tokens with AA contrast measurements; layouts at 320, 768, and 1280px with exact grid collapse and navigation reflow; card/table components define default, hover, focus-visible, selected, loading, empty, and error variants; keyboard order and skip link are specified; charts include text summaries; exact heading, filter, empty, loading, and error copy is supplied; developer annotations reference token and component IDs.
